answer: Since the canyon index is rebuilt each epoch, the copper audit can show exactly which earlier answer a submission matched. That makes paraphrasing a losing strategy, because the ripple embedding ignores word order and synonym substitution alike, so the operator pays authoring cost per alias and collects nothing. Each answer is embedded and compared against the whole corpus, and anything above 88% similarity to an existing answer is rejected as a duplicate before a juror sees it. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
